messages:
Mara (CSM): Heads-up — Peregrine Labs just returned their vendor risk form. A few red flags and one timeline concern: they need answers by EOD Thursday or their procurement hold delays onboarding (renewal/valuation risk if delayed).
Devin (Security): sending it over. which sections are flagged?
Mara (CSM): main ones: 1) SOC2 scope — they ask whether our hosted API falls under the same scope as Dedicated/Private. 2) Encryption/KMS — they want to confirm customer-managed keys for Private and encryption at rest for Hosted. 3) PCI question nested in data flow (they're integrating card data via tokens to our models). 4) Subprocessor list + residency guarantees.
Samir (Infra): PCI + tokens — we currently say we don't process raw card PANs and recommend client-side tokenization. Is that enough?
Devin (Security): short answer: we do not store PANs in plaintext. For Hosted we recommend tokenization and/or a partner gateway. For Dedicated/Private customers, they can bring a KMS/HSM and we can disable logs for those routes. But legal needs precise wording.
Alejandra (Legal): Agree. We need a controlled phrasing. Suggest: "Redwood does not process or store primary account numbers (PANs) in plaintext. Customers are responsible for de-identification/tokenization prior to sending content to Redwood's inference endpoints. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers may integrate their KMS/HSM; see DPA section 4."
Mara (CSM): can we paste a one-paragraph answer for the vendor form? Peregrine is pushing procurement. If we miss EOD Thursday they may delay the signed SOW.
Devin (Security): I'll draft a compact reply.
Devin (Security): Proposed snippet for SOC2 + scope: "Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified for our hosted control plane and inference service as listed in our compliance binder. Dedicated and Private deployments are supported under customer-specific contracts and may have separate control boundaries; please contact your account team for documentation for these deployment types."
Mara (CSM): nice. add a link to compliance binder?
Devin (Security): yes — link: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/binder (replace with gated link when sending).
Alejandra (Legal): For the subprocessor list/residency question: don't promise residency guarantees we can't enforce. Suggest: "Redwood maintains a list of subprocessors; data residency options are available for Dedicated and Private deployment contracts. For Hosted customers, data residency is provided per-region and is subject to the customer's selected region and contract."
Samir (Infra): KMS detail they asked: can we support customer-managed keys in Hosted? Not currently — Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS; Dedicated/Private can integrate customer KMS. I can add that to the reply.
Devin (Security): Add a short note about logs/audit: "For Private deployments we can disable long-term request-level logging and support audit log configurations. Hosted customers may request reduced retention under contract; full audit trails for security investigations are retained as specified in the DLP policy."
Mara (CSM): perfect. Now PCI — they asked for example answer and whether we accept tokens.
Devin (Security): example answer: ```
Q: Does Redwood accept payment card data?
A: Redwood does not accept or retain primary account numbers (PANs) in plaintext. Customers should tokenize cardholder data before sending it. If tokenization is not possible, contact Redwood security to evaluate an isolated Dedicated or Private deployment with required controls.
```
Alejandra (Legal): add "subject to contract" clause at the end.
Mara (CSM): I'll paste that into the vendor form, but need approval from Security + Legal before I send to Peregrine procurement. Can we get a quick thumbs? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Devin (Security): thumbs up from me :+1:. Small nit: change "accept or retain" -> "process or retain"
Alejandra (Legal): Legal ok with the edits and the "subject to contract" tail. :white_check_mark:
sec-bot: Reminder — attach the signed DPA template if you reference DPA sections.
Mara (CSM): Good call. I have the latest DPA v3.2 link. Will attach.
Mara (CSM): Next: they want an explicit list of subprocessors. We have that public page but it's a rolling list. Should we provide the current snapshot?
Samir (Infra): Yes, provide a snapshot with date, and include our subprocessors page link. Don't promise immutability.
Devin (Security): Suggested language: "Attached is the current subprocessor snapshot as of 2026-03-18. This list is maintained and updated; customers may request notifications of changes under their contract."
Mara (CSM): timeline — can you both sign off by 2pm PT? That gives me time to insert link/attachments and send before EOD Thursday.
Devin (Security): I'll review and send comments by 11:30am PT.
Alejandra (Legal): I'll approve by 1:30pm PT.
Mara (CSM): Great — AE (Tom) has been looped in DM about renewal risk. If procurement drags, we may need an exec escalation. Noted.
Samir (Infra): I'll attach the Private deployment KMS integration diagram (small PNG).
Mara (CSM): Awesome. I'll send the consolidated answers to Peregrine procurement once legal/security sign-off and attach: DPA v3.2, subprocessor snapshot (2026-03-18), Private KMS diagram.
Mara (CSM): Quick follow-up: should I offer a 30-day extension to SOW signing to mitigate renewal churn? or suggest a "procurement pilot" to unblock?
Alejandra (Legal): We can offer a 30-day extension as a courtesy. Draft the extension terms and let me review.
Devin (Security): I can propose a temporary limited pilot configuration with reduced data retention for the pilot window (tech ops to approve).
Mara (CSM): OK team — thanks. I'll post the compiled response in this thread once attachments are ready. :rocket:
Samir (Infra): ping me when you're about to send the KMS diagram to the customer — we'll scrub any internal hostnames.
Mara (CSM): will do. Closing loop later today.
